evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Chooses composition (app.root) over inheritance from tk.Tk, presents the application object graph, and separates pure domain logic from UI logic.

Inheriting from tk.Tk works but is unnecessary; app.root composition matches how chapter 16's apps were built. -- confirmed -- chapter 16.24/16.25 and the Tip Calculator Pro (16.31) and notes editor (16.30) all use the app-holds-root pattern; those pages verified to exist. tic_tac_toe.py takes root as a constructor parameter, consistent with the claim.

The app holds the widgets and a reference to the state, not the other way round. -- confirmed -- TicTacToeApp holds self.root, self.state, self.buttons, self.status_var, self.score_var; GameState holds no reference back to the app or any widget.

find_winner(board), is_draw(board) and the index arithmetic are domain logic; attempt_move, on_cell_enter/leave, render, new_round/new_match are UI logic. -- confirmed -- the three domain functions were called successfully with no Tk root in existence, while the UI methods require a live app; the comparison table matches the real file's structure.

The test 'can it be checked without opening a window?' distinguishes the two layers. -- confirmed -- exactly the property exercised in 17.28 and notebook 17-28, which runs the full rules matrix with no window.
